pending_commit.commit_message: shill: Add mockable keyword In general, the virtual keyword is used for methods that are going to be mocked, even if those methods should not be inherited by non-mock children. This works fine for projects that have a flat or very simple inheritance hierarchy. Shill, however, has neither of those, and the most complex inheritance hierarchies (e.g. the Service and Device hierarchies) become much more difficult to read and understand when one is never sure if a virtual method is used just for mocks or is also overridden by children. This change creates a separate 'mockable' keyword for methods that should only be overridden by mocks. The 'mockable' behavior is enforced by being #defined to virtual only in test builds. BUG=chromium:997295 TEST=None. cryptohome: Abort chall-resp mount on ROCA-vuln TPMs Refuse to create/mount challenge-response protected home dirs (a.k.a. smart card login users) when the TPM chip is known to be ROCA-vulnerable. This allows to avoid the unnoticeable security degradation of the strength of the user data protection in the situation where the code can easily detect this weakness. For the background, the challenge-response protection heavily relies on the TPM capabilities. If the TPM is vulnerable and the hardware-backed secrets can be decrypted by an attacker, the only level of the user data protection is the encryption based on a cryptographic signature of a constant per-user salt - which is significantly weaker than the hardware-backed protection.
